statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 21%, four points below the block threshold, after the jobless-claims print cleared without a directional impulse and NQ held a 463-point range at 30,819.50, roughly 328 points under its session high, while the just-begun cash open has no verified price path yet, the 14:00Z ISM release is still ahead, and a 24-year-high long-end yield keeps Stress at 75%.
recommendation: Tail moves one point to 21% and stays inside the watch band. The structural evidence is benign. At 13:19Z NQ futures traded 30,819.50, up 0.39% from a 30,698.75 previous close, inside a session range of 30,684.50 to 31,147.75; price sits about 328 points below that high and 135 above the low, so the 463-point range has produced a large, completed retracement rather than session-extreme holding. VIX is unchanged at 16.34 near its 16.21 session low. Initial jobless claims for the week ending 26 September printed 197,000 against a 200,000 to 201,000 consensus, down 1,000 from a prior week revised to 198,000, with the four-week average at 200,000 and continuing claims at 1,701,000, the lowest in three years; the release produced no measurable directional impulse, repeating the 7 August pattern in which a labour-market surprise did not become a no-retracement path. Against that, the cross-asset backdrop is genuinely stressed. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.342% intraday, its highest since early 2002, and trades near 5.319%, while the 30-year is around 5.676% and European and UK long ends are also at multi-decade highs; the 2-year is lower at 4.873%, so the move is a long-end, term-premium event rather than a repricing of near-term policy. Brent for December has reclaimed roughly 100 dollars, up about 2%, after Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports outside Hong Kong and Macau into a Gulf market still structurally impaired. Equities are absorbing both: Micron's fiscal Q4 beat, 33.42 dollars adjusted on 54.23 billion in revenue with first-quarter guidance near 61.5 billion, has supported semiconductors and megacaps, with Alphabet up about 2.2%. That combination of a severe bond move alongside a resilient, range-respecting equity tape is a conflict, and under this contract conflict raises Stress rather than Tail. Stress therefore moves to 75%, high rather than extreme. Two checkpoints sit inside the danger window: the 13:30Z cash open, which has just begun with no verified post-open price path yet, and the 14:00Z ISM Manufacturing release, consensus near 54.7 against a 55 prior, with Construction Spending alongside it. Confidence is 88%: current verified levels are held for NQ, VIX, the 2-year and 10-year, Brent and WTI, the claims actual and the seven-day calendar, with the gap being an absence of verified post-open price path and an unhealthy shared context file.
headline: Tail 21% at watch after claims clear without impulse; 24-year-high yields hold Stress at 75%
body: The observed Nasdaq-100 picture at 13:19Z is a market that is absorbing stress rather than trending through it. NQ futures at 30,819.50 are 0.39% higher on the day but about 328 points below the 31,147.75 session high, with the 30,684.50 low intact; a large retracement has already completed inside a 463-point range, and there is no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after a failed retracement and no holding of a session extreme. VIX is flat at 16.34. Initial jobless claims came in at 197,000 against a consensus near 200,000, the lowest since mid-July, with continuing claims at 1,701,000, a three-year low; the tape did not react directionally, which is the clearest available evidence against the pathological price path that the Tail score measures. The stress channel is the global bond market. The US 10-year yield touched 5.342%, the highest since early 2002, as a worldwide government-debt sell-off deepened, with the 30-year near 5.676% and French, Italian, UK and Japanese long ends also at multi-decade highs; the US 2-year is lower on the day at 4.873%, so this is a term-premium and supply story rather than a near-term policy repricing. Energy reinforces it: Brent for December is back around 100 dollars, up roughly 2%, after Chinese refiners suspended October product exports outside Hong Kong and Macau during a national holiday week, on top of a Strait of Hormuz disruption that analysts expect to persist. Offsetting that, Micron's fiscal fourth quarter beat substantially at 33.42 dollars adjusted on 54.23 billion in revenue with guidance near 61.5 billion, supporting semiconductors and the AI complex, and megacap breadth is positive with Alphabet up about 2.2% though Apple is marginally lower. Rising long-end yields alongside a firm equity tape is a conflict rather than an alignment, and conflicting cross-asset evidence raises Stress and uncertainty rather than Tail. Tail therefore sits at 21%, one point higher than the previous hour and four below the block threshold, reflecting two near-term checkpoints rather than observed structure: the 13:30Z US cash open, which has just begun without a verified post-open price path yet, and the 14:00Z ISM Manufacturing PMI with consensus near 54.7 against a 55 prior, released together with Construction Spending. A narrow danger window of 13:30Z to 15:00Z covers the opening auction and the ISM reaction. The forecast path assumes orderly two-way discovery and decays Tail into the US close and the Asian session, then rebuilds it through Friday morning toward the 12:30Z September employment report, where consensus is about 90,000 payrolls and a 4.1% unemployment rate. Under this contract the size of a payrolls surprise does not by itself establish a pathological path; only the observed price reaction does, and a bond-led delayed second leg is the credible amplifier to monitor given where long-end yields are trading. Evidence here comes from independent current research. Dominant mode is mixed.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hours Claude published a continuous watch-band regime. Tail ran between 20% and 25%, briefly touching the 25% block threshold in the 06:00Z hour on a trend-up reading before easing back to 20-22% once that structure failed to persist. Stress rose steadily from 67% to a 76% peak as the global bond sell-off and the energy complex tightened, and sits at 74-75% in the most recent hours. Confidence held in a narrow 87-89% band throughout. Dominant mode was mixed for 22 of the 24 slots.
outlookSummary: The near path is governed by two unobserved checkpoints inside the current hour and the next: the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:00Z ISM Manufacturing PMI with Construction Spending. Tail is projected to peak at 23% in the 14:00Z release hour, then decay through the US afternoon to 19% at the cash close and to a 15% trough across the Asian session, where Chinese holiday closures thin regional flow. It rebuilds from 16% at the European reopen to 24% in the 12:00Z hour on Friday, which contains the US September employment report. Every forecast value above the current hour is conditional risk for a scheduled checkpoint, not an assertion that directional structure has been observed. The projected path assumes orderly two-way price discovery, no new geopolitical discontinuity, and no sustained acceleration of the long-end yield move into equities.
